title: Removing Unnecessary and Counterproductive Restrictions on Access to Federal Lands

enrichment.summary: This executive order rescinds two previous orders that imposed vague and restrictive rules on off-road vehicle use on federal lands. It directs federal agencies to revise regulations to increase public access to federal lands, streamline management, and reduce unnecessary regulatory burdens while maintaining existing statutory environmental protections.
potential_concerns: Increased off-road vehicle access may lead to degradation of natural habitats and disruption of wildlife, adversely affecting environmental justice communities and tribal communities reliant on these lands for cultural and subsistence activities.

Streamlining regulations to reduce barriers for energy and timber production could prioritize industrial access over conservation, potentially harming rural communities whose economies and lifestyles depend on healthy ecosystems.

Rescinding prior environmental safeguards may unintentionally increase conflicts among recreational users, particularly disadvantaging hikers and non-motorized recreationists who may experience reduced access or safety concerns.

Reducing regulatory restrictions could lead to faster permitting processes that benefit energy-sector workers but increase risks of environmental damage that disproportionately impact tribal and rural communities.
